title: Bones of the pelvis (anterior)
attribution: 3D anatomy from Z-Anatomy, built on BodyParts3D (CC BY-SA). Rendered in Blender; surface detail added with an image model.

rows: Five fused vertebrae forming the back of the pelvis, between the two hip bones.
L5 above, the coccyx below, and the ilium on each side at the sacroiliac joint.
Sacral promontory, anterior and posterior sacral foramina, the sacral canal, and the sacral hiatus.
Three to five small fused vertebrae at the lower end of the vertebral column (the tailbone).
Gives attachment to gluteus maximus, the muscles of the pelvic floor, and the anococcygeal ligament.
Midline joint between the bodies of the two pubic bones.
A disc of fibrocartilage (the interpubic disc), strengthened by the superior and inferior pubic ligaments.
Holds the front of the pelvic ring together and allows a little movement. It loosens in late pregnancy.
Upper, fan-shaped part of the hip bone.
Sacrum, at the sacroiliac joint, and the head of the femur, at the acetabulum (hip joint). It fuses with the ischium and pubis at the acetabulum.
Iliac crest, anterior superior and anterior inferior iliac spines, iliac fossa, auricular surface, and the greater sciatic notch.
hy: A line joining the tops of the two iliac crests crosses the spine at about L4, the landmark for a lumbar puncture.

rows: Lower, posterior part of the hip bone.
Head of the femur, at the acetabulum (hip joint). It fuses with the ilium and pubis at the acetabulum, and its ramus joins the inferior ramus of the pubis.
Ischial tuberosity, which bears the weight in sitting and gives origin to the hamstrings; ischial spine; lesser sciatic notch.
hy: The ischial spine is the landmark for a pudendal nerve block.

rows: Anterior, lower part of the hip bone.
The opposite pubis, at the pubic symphysis, and the head of the femur, at the acetabulum (hip joint). It fuses with the ilium and ischium at the acetabulum.
Body, superior and inferior rami, pubic crest, and pubic tubercle, where the inguinal ligament attaches. With the ischium it surrounds the obturator foramen.
